section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the need to understand the connection between guarding Israel like the pupil of an eye and the eagle stirring its nest, and begins by citing the Baal HaHilula's discourse on the verse "את הוי' האמרת היום" and the question of the Ohr HaChayim about the repetition of keeping commandments.
section.t: And to understand this,
and also to understand the relevance of the matters that through this—that He guards him like the pupil of His eye—through this, "as an eagle stirs its nest,"
and through this, "He carries him on His pinions, Hashem alone leads him,"
this will be understood by prefacing a discourse of the Baal HaHilulah
on the verse
"את הוי' האמרת today... and הוי' האמירך today..."
And he brings what is said in the continuation of the verse, "and הוי' האמירך today... to guard all His commandments,"
about which the holy Ohr HaChayim asked: is this not a matter of the condition of honor that is inscribed in Israel's actions toward Hashem,
as it is written in the verse, "את הוי' האמרת today... and to guard His statutes and commandments...,"
so what place is there to mention it in the matters from Hashem to Israel?
But the matter will be understood by prefacing the explanation of "האמרת" and "האמירך" as an expression of praise,
as the teaching of Chazal
on this verse,
"The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Israel: You have made Me a unique entity in the world, and I will make you a unique entity in the world."
"You have made Me a unique entity in the world, as it is said,
'Hear O Israel, Hashem our G-d, Hashem is One.'
And I will make you a unique entity in the world, as it is said,
'And who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land.'"

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that "האמרת" has three meanings—praise, garment, and speech—and connects them to Rosh Hashanah, where Israel coronates Hashem, He dons the garment of kingship, and the world of speech is built.
section.t: And one may add what is explained elsewhere,
that "האמרת" has three explanations,
the first explanation,
an expression of praise,
as above,
the second explanation,
an expression of a garment,
a purple robe,
as it says in the Midrash
on the verse
"בצע אמרתו,"
"He tore the purple robe
(garment)
of His."
And the third explanation,
from the expression of speech and utterance.
And this is the relevance of the verse "את הוי' האמרת today..." to Rosh Hashanah,
for,
it is explained in Likkutei Torah
that "the day" unqualified refers to Rosh Hashanah,
and on Rosh Hashanah the matter of "את הוי' האמרת today" is accomplished,
in all three explanations above.
For, behold,
the service of Rosh Hashanah is as Chazal said,
"The Holy One, blessed be He, said
(to Israel),
'Recite before Me on Rosh Hashanah Kingship verses... so that you may coronate Me over you,'"
and this is the content of the first explanation of "האמרת,"
an expression of praise,
which is the matter of "You have made Me a unique entity in the world, as it is said, 'Hear O Israel, Hashem our G-d, Hashem is One,'"
as Chazal said,
"'Hear O Israel, Hashem our G-d, Hashem is One'—this is Kingship."
And the second explanation,
an expression of a garment,
for when Adam HaRishon was created on Rosh Hashanah, it says, "Hashem is King, He is clothed in majesty,"
that He was clothed in the garment of kingship.
And the third explanation, an expression of speech and utterance,
as is known,
that on Rosh Hashanah is the building of the world of speech.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section elaborates on the three explanations of "One" in the praise of "Hashem is One" and "one nation," explaining that it negates any equal, negates idolatry, and commands the unique unification of Hashem that is specific to Israel.
section.t: And he continues in the discourse
in explaining the explanation of "האמרת" and "האמירך" as an expression of praise,
that in both of them "one" is said
("Hashem is One,"
"one nation"),
which has three explanations.
The first explanation,
as Chazal said,
"One—there is none like Him."
And one must understand: what is the praise that there is none like Him?
How could it enter one's mind that there is one like Him, G-d forbid?
For even the nations of the world call Him "G-d of gods,"
so why is it necessary to say that there is none like Him?
And the second explanation,
that "one" negates the matter of idolatry,
as Chazal said,
"From where did Israel merit the Shema? From the Giving of the Torah.
The Holy One, blessed be He, said, 'Hear O Israel, I am Hashem your G-d.' Israel answered, 'Hashem our G-d.'
'You shall have no other gods...' Israel answered, 'Hashem is One.'
And it is found,
that 'Hashem our G-d, Hashem is One' is an acceptance of the two commandments of 'I am' and 'You shall have no other gods,'
and that is,
that 'one' negates the matter of idolatry.
And the third explanation,
that 'Hashem is One' is a commandment in itself,
the commandment to unify Him,
for it is possible to fulfill the command of 'I am' and 'You shall have no other gods,'
and nevertheless,
this is not yet the matter of unification,
and upon this is added the matter of 'Hashem is One,'
which is the commandment to unify Him,
and it is the negation of the matter of partnership,
about which the Children of Israel were commanded in the verse, 'Hear O Israel... Hashem is One,'
unlike the nations of the world,
for even though they were commanded concerning idolatry,
as it says regarding Adam HaRishon, 'and He commanded,'
and Chazal said,
'There is no "command" but idolatry,'
nevertheless,
they were not commanded concerning partnership
(as the Rema wrote,
who follows the Ran and the Tosafos).
And that is,
that among the nations of the world,
including even the righteous gentiles,
there is no matter of the belief in unification,
for it is specifically in Israel alone.
